name.en: DIAMUN 2027 (Dubai International Academy Model United Nations)
name.ka: DIAMUN 2027 (Dubai International Academy-ის გაეროს მოდელი)
name.ar: مؤتمر DIAMUN 2027 لنموذج الأمم المتحدة في دبي

grades: primary and secondary (school delegations and individuals)
deadline_note: School registration form deadline 15 Dec 2026; final delegate names (Form II) due 8 Jan 2027, per diamun.org.

summary.en: The 19th DIAMUN, the largest student-led THIMUN-affiliated MUN in the MENA region, runs 5–7 February 2027 in Dubai with around 800 delegates. Schools, individual secondary and primary delegates, chairs and press can all register.
summary.ka: მე-19 DIAMUN — MENA რეგიონში ყველაზე დიდი სტუდენტების მიერ მართული, THIMUN-თან აფილირებული გაეროს მოდელი — 2027 წლის 5–7 თებერვალს დუბაიში ჩატარდება, დაახლოებით 800 დელეგატით. რეგისტრაცია ღიაა სკოლებისთვის, ინდივიდუალური დელეგატებისთვის, თავმჯდომარეებისა და პრესისთვის.
summary.ar: تُعقد النسخة التاسعة عشرة من DIAMUN، أكبر مؤتمر لنموذج الأمم المتحدة يديره الطلاب ومنتسب إلى THIMUN في المنطقة، من 5 إلى 7 فبراير 2027 في دبي بمشاركة نحو 800 مندوب. يمكن للمدارس والمندوبين الأفراد من المرحلتين الابتدائية والثانوية والرؤساء والصحافة التسجيل.

about.en:
DIAMUN is the annual Model United Nations conference of Dubai International Academy and describes itself as the largest student-led, THIMUN-affiliated MUN in the Middle East and North Africa. The 19th edition runs 5–7 February 2027 at the DIA Emirates Hills campus in Dubai, with the opening ceremony on 4 February at the Al Barsha campus. Its theme is "Better Together: Reconstructing Global Governance in an Era of Fragmentation", and roughly 800 delegates from more than 50 international schools are expected.

The conference runs more than fifteen committees split into General Assemblies and Specialised Committees, with options for beginner, intermediate and advanced delegates, so no prior MUN experience is needed. Debate follows THIMUN procedure (resolution writing, lobbying, debate and voting) and covers economic, social and political issues, building public speaking, research, writing and negotiation skills.

Schools register a delegation through a director or teacher, but there are also forms for external individual secondary delegates, primary-school delegates, chairs/student officers and press. Fees include conference registration, lunch and the social event; travel and accommodation are your own. It is one of the best-organised school MUNs in the Gulf and a good first international MUN for students in the region.

en: About 800 delegates from 50+ schools; THIMUN-affiliated
Committees for beginner, intermediate and advanced delegates, plus a primary-school track
Individual delegates can register, not only school delegations

eligibility.en: Primary and secondary school students. Schools register through an MUN director/teacher; external students may register as individual secondary or primary delegates. Chair applications for 2027 are closed. Conducted in English. Open to any nationality.

en: Choose the right form on the DIAMUN 2027 registration page (school delegation, individual secondary or primary delegate, press).
Submit Form I by 15 December 2026; you receive portal login details by email.
Directors pay the school and director fees, then complete Form II with final delegate names by 8 January 2027.
Pay delegate fees in AED via the portal (fees are non-refundable from 8 January 2027).
Prepare position papers/resolutions for your committee before 5 February.

costs.en: School registration fee AED 1,050 (incl. VAT); secondary delegate or advisor AED 630; primary delegate, press, student officer or admin AED 315. Covers registration, conference lunch and social event; not travel, accommodation or other meals.

score_reason: Large, well-run THIMUN-affiliated school MUN in Dubai; open to individuals; registration open until mid-December.

org: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST)

name.ka: KAUST-ის მოწვეული სტუდენტის კვლევითი პროგრამა (VSRP)
name.ar: برنامج الطلاب الزائرين للبحث في كاوست (VSRP)

duration.ar: من شهرين إلى 6 أشهر، بداية مرنة

deadline_note: Rolling: applications accepted year-round with flexible start dates (admissions.kaust.edu.sa).

summary.en: A fully funded 2–6 month STEM research internship at KAUST on the Red Sea coast, with a USD 1,000 monthly stipend, flights and private housing. Undergraduates in year 3+ and master's students from any country can apply year-round.
summary.ka: სრულად დაფინანსებული 2–6-თვიანი STEM კვლევითი სტაჟირება KAUST-ში, წითელი ზღვის სანაპიროზე: თვეში 1000 აშშ დოლარი სტიპენდია, ავიაბილეთები და ცალკე საცხოვრებელი. განაცხადი მთელი წლის განმავლობაში მიიღება ნებისმიერი ქვეყნის მე-3 კურსიდან ბაკალავრებისა და მაგისტრანტებისგან.
summary.ar: تدريب بحثي ممول بالكامل في مجالات العلوم والتقنية لمدة 2 إلى 6 أشهر في كاوست على ساحل البحر الأحمر، مع مكافأة شهرية قدرها 1000 دولار وتذاكر طيران وسكن خاص. يقبل البرنامج طلبات طلاب البكالوريوس من السنة الثالثة فما فوق وطلاب الماجستير من أي دولة طوال العام.

about.en:
The Visiting Student Research Program (VSRP) lets undergraduate and master's students spend two to six months doing real research in a KAUST lab in Thuwal, Saudi Arabia. KAUST lists more than 100 faculty-led projects across science, engineering, computing, AI, marine science, energy and the environment; you pick a project and work with that faculty member's group, with access to KAUST's core laboratories.

It is fully funded: a USD 1,000 monthly stipend, a private bedroom and bathroom on campus, return airfare, campus facilities and social and cultural activities. Applications are accepted all year with flexible start and end dates, and there is no application fee. Many students use it as a route into KAUST's fully funded MS and PhD programmes.

You need to be at least a third-year undergraduate or a master's student (recent graduates within a year also qualify), with a GPA of at least 3.5/4 and proof of English proficiency. You apply to one project at a time with transcripts, a statement of purpose, a CV, your passport and one faculty recommendation.

en: USD 1,000/month stipend, flights and private campus housing
100+ faculty-led STEM projects; flexible 2–6 month duration
Rolling admissions and no application fee

eligibility.en: Third-year or higher undergraduates and master's students of any nationality (or graduates within one year of the start date). Minimum GPA 3.5/4 or equivalent. English proficiency proof (IELTS, TOEFL, PTE, Cambridge C1/C2 or Duolingo) unless exempt. Current PhD students and KAUST students/alumni are not eligible.

en: Browse the VSRP project list on the KAUST admissions site and choose one project.
Click Apply on that project page (one application at a time).
Upload English transcripts, a statement of purpose, CV and passport (6+ months validity).
Name one faculty recommender; KAUST contacts them directly.
Wait for a decision (KAUST decides on a rolling basis).

costs.en: Free to apply. Fully funded: USD 1,000 monthly stipend, private housing, return airfare and campus access.

score_reason: Fully funded, open to all nationalities, rolling; excellent research experience.

org: Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence (MBZUAI)

name.ka: MBZUAI-ის გლობალური კვლევითი სტაჟირება (MGRIP) 2027
name.ar: برنامج MBZUAI العالمي للتدريب البحثي (MGRIP) 2027

deadline_note: Application window 1 Jan – 28 Feb 2027 (5 pm GST); decisions by 2 Apr 2027, per MBZUAI MGRIP page. 2027 projects released in November 2026.

summary.en: MBZUAI's month-long summer AI research internship in Abu Dhabi, the successor to its UGRIP programme, now open to undergraduate and master's students worldwide. Interns work in teams on faculty-led AI projects in machine learning, computer vision and NLP.
summary.ka: MBZUAI-ის ერთთვიანი საზაფხულო კვლევითი სტაჟირება ხელოვნურ ინტელექტში აბუ-დაბიში — UGRIP-ის მემკვიდრე, რომელიც ახლა მთელი მსოფლიოს ბაკალავრებსა და მაგისტრანტებს იღებს. სტაჟიორები გუნდურად მუშაობენ პროფესორების ხელმძღვანელობით მანქანურ სწავლებაში, კომპიუტერულ ხედვასა და NLP-ში.
summary.ar: تدريب بحثي صيفي في الذكاء الاصطناعي لمدة شهر في أبوظبي تقدمه جامعة محمد بن زايد للذكاء الاصطناعي، وهو خليفة برنامج UGRIP، ومفتوح الآن لطلاب البكالوريوس والماجستير من جميع أنحاء العالم. يعمل المتدربون ضمن فرق على مشاريع يقودها أعضاء هيئة التدريس في تعلم الآلة والرؤية الحاسوبية ومعالجة اللغات.

about.en:
MBZUAI, the world's first graduate university dedicated to artificial intelligence, runs a four-week research internship on its Abu Dhabi campus each summer. Previously called the Undergraduate Research Internship Program (UGRIP), it has been renamed the MBZUAI Global Research Internship Program (MGRIP) and widened to undergraduate and master's students from around the world. The 2027 edition runs 7 June to 2 July 2027.

Interns join small teams working on faculty-led projects across machine learning, computer vision, natural language processing, robotics and related areas, attend lectures and workshops, and present their results at the end. Past UGRIP cohorts were hosted on campus with travel and accommodation provided; check the MGRIP page for the 2027 funding terms. The 2027 project list is due to be published in November 2026.

Applications open 1 January 2027 and close 28 February 2027, with decisions by 2 April. In the previous cycle applicants needed a STEM-related major, a CGPA of at least 3.5/4 and an approved English test score. It is a strong option for students considering MBZUAI's fully funded MSc and PhD programmes.

en: Four weeks of hands-on AI research on MBZUAI's Abu Dhabi campus
Open worldwide to undergraduate and master's students
Pathway towards MBZUAI's fully funded graduate programmes

eligibility.en: Undergraduate and master's students from any country. The previous cycle required a STEM-related major, CGPA 3.5/4 or higher and an approved English test; confirm 2027 requirements on the MGRIP page.

en: Check the 2027 project list on the MGRIP page (released November 2026).
Prepare transcripts, CV, English test score and statement.
Apply online between 1 January and 28 February 2027 (5 pm GST).
Receive a decision by 2 April 2027.

costs.en: No tuition. Earlier editions covered travel and on-campus accommodation for interns; confirm the 2027 package on the official page.

score_reason: Prestigious AI research internship open worldwide; window opens January 2027.

org: King Abdulaziz and His Companions Foundation for Giftedness and Creativity (Mawhiba)

name.en: Mawhiba National Gifted Olympiad 2027 (Ibdaa research track & Nasmu science track)
name.ka: Mawhiba-ს ეროვნული ნიჭიერთა ოლიმპიადა 2027 (Ibdaa კვლევითი და Nasmu სამეცნიერო მიმართულებები)
name.ar: أولمبياد موهبة الوطني 2027 (المسار البحثي إبداع والمسار العلمي نسمو)

deadline_note: Mawhiba lists 2 Nov 2026 for Ibdaa registration (page countdown on 29 Oct showed 3 days left). Nasmu registration is through school coordinators.

summary.en: Saudi Arabia's national olympiad for gifted students, combining the Ibdaa research-project fair (pathway to ISEF) and the Nasmu science olympiad track (pathway to international olympiad teams). Registration is free.
summary.ka: საუდის არაბეთის ეროვნული ოლიმპიადა ნიჭიერი მოსწავლეებისთვის, რომელიც აერთიანებს Ibdaa-ს კვლევით პროექტების ფესტივალს (გზა ISEF-მდე) და Nasmu-ს სამეცნიერო ოლიმპიადას (გზა საერთაშორისო ოლიმპიადების გუნდებამდე). რეგისტრაცია უფასოა.
summary.ar: الأولمبياد الوطني للموهوبين في المملكة، ويجمع بين معرض المشاريع البحثية «إبداع» (الطريق إلى معرض ISEF) والمسار العلمي «نسمو» (الطريق إلى فرق الأولمبيادات الدولية). التسجيل مجاني.

about.en:
Mawhiba's National Gifted Olympiad is the main gateway for Saudi school students into international science competitions. It has two tracks under one framework. Ibdaa, the research track, is a national science and engineering fair: students submit an individual research project, attend training lectures, go through online judging, present at regional exhibitions and, if they qualify, at the national exhibition, which selects the Saudi delegation to the Regeneron International Science and Engineering Fair (ISEF).

Nasmu, the science track, is an olympiad pathway in mathematics, science, informatics (C++), physics, chemistry and biology. Students sit an electronic test, a national-team test, then training camps with central tests and finals; finalists join Saudi national-team preparation for international olympiads (IMO, IPhO, IChO, IBO, IOI, AI and more). Saudi students compete in more than 29 international olympiads and fairs through this route.

Both tracks are free, and participation does not affect the regular school track. Training days, exhibitions and tests are in person. Ibdaa winners receive prizes, and every finalist receives a certificate.

en: Free; the official pathway to ISEF and international science olympiads for Saudi students
Two tracks: Ibdaa (individual research projects) and Nasmu (olympiad subjects)
Training lectures, regional and national exhibitions, national-team camps

eligibility.en: Ibdaa: Saudi nationals in intermediate or secondary general education, aged 11–20, one individual project each. Nasmu: students from first intermediate to first secondary grade (subject-specific), registered through their school coordinator. In person in Saudi Arabia.

en: Log in to the Mawhiba website or app and confirm your profile.
For Ibdaa, register through the National Gifted Olympiad service before the deadline and submit your project and documents.
For Nasmu, register through your school's olympiad coordinator.
Attend the training lectures and the electronic tests or judging.
Qualifiers present at central exhibitions or attend national-team camps.

costs.en: Free registration. In-person attendance at training days and exhibitions is required (travel within Saudi Arabia at your own cost unless Mawhiba states otherwise).

score_reason: Free flagship olympiad and ISEF pathway, but Ibdaa limited to Saudi nationals and deadline is imminent.

org: Mawhiba

name.ka: Bebras Mawhiba — გამოთვლითი აზროვნების შეჯიბრი 2026
name.ar: مسابقة بيبراس موهبة للتفكير الحاسوبي 2026

deadline_note: Registration ends 26 Nov 2026 per the Mawhiba service page; test dates on bebrasksa.org.

summary.en: The Saudi edition of the international Bebras challenge: a remote, 10-problem computational-thinking test in Arabic or English for students from grade 3 to grade 12. No programming experience is needed.
summary.ka: საერთაშორისო Bebras-ის საუდის ვერსია: დისტანციური, 10-ამოცანიანი გამოთვლითი აზროვნების ტესტი არაბულ ან ინგლისურ ენაზე მე-3–მე-12 კლასის მოსწავლეებისთვის. პროგრამირების გამოცდილება საჭირო არ არის.
summary.ar: النسخة السعودية من تحدي بيبراس الدولي: اختبار عن بُعد من 10 مسائل في التفكير الحاسوبي باللغتين العربية أو الإنجليزية للطلاب من الصف الثالث الابتدائي حتى الثالث الثانوي، ولا يتطلب خبرة برمجية.

about.en:
Bebras is one of the world's largest informatics and computational-thinking challenges, run in more than 60 countries. Mawhiba organises the Saudi edition, Bebras Mawhiba, as a fully remote test for students from grade 3 of primary through grade 3 of secondary school.

The test has 10 interactive problems, each with four levels of increasing difficulty (maximum 400 points). Problems test logic, algorithms, patterns and data reasoning rather than coding, so no programming background is needed, and it can be taken in Arabic or English. Students get one attempt, see results immediately after the test, and winners receive medals delivered via their regional education departments.

It is an accessible first competition for younger students and a good warm-up for the informatics olympiad track. The official site has a Bebras library with sample problems for practice.

en: Remote, in Arabic or English, no coding needed
10 interactive problems with four difficulty levels
Medals for winners; good entry point to informatics olympiads

eligibility.en: Students from grade 3 primary to grade 3 secondary enrolled in general education inside Saudi Arabia (any nationality).

en: Log in to the Bebras Mawhiba website (bebrasksa.org) and confirm your profile.
Register through the service system and accept the terms.
Pay the SAR 60 contribution before 26 November 2026.
Practise with the Bebras library, then take the test on the scheduled date.

costs.en: SAR 60 guardian contribution (Apple Pay, mada, Visa, Mastercard).

score_reason: Accessible, cheap remote contest, but limited to students in Saudi schools.

org: Mawhiba

name.en: Mawhiba Tamayuz Programme for Admission to Top Universities
name.ka: Mawhiba-ს Tamayuz — მომზადება წამყვან უნივერსიტეტებში ჩასაბარებლად
name.ar: برنامج موهبة للالتحاق بالجامعات المرموقة «التميز»

duration.en: Grade 11 to university applications (about one year)
duration.ar: من الصف الثاني الثانوي حتى التقديم للجامعات (نحو عام)

deadline_note: Mawhiba lists 3 Nov 2026 for Tamayuz registration (countdown on page). Verify before applying.

summary.en: Mawhiba's preparation programme that trains second-year secondary students in Saudi Arabia to apply to top-50 universities in the United States, with SAT training, essay coaching and application support. Admitted students then apply for sponsorship from partners such as the Ministry of Education, KAUST and Aramco.
summary.ka: Mawhiba-ს პროგრამა, რომელიც საუდის არაბეთის მე-11 კლასის მოსწავლეებს ამზადებს აშშ-ის ტოპ-50 უნივერსიტეტებში ჩასაბარებლად: SAT-ის მომზადება, ესეების წერა და განაცხადის მხარდაჭერა. ჩარიცხვის შემდეგ სტუდენტები დაფინანსებას პარტნიორებთან ითხოვენ (განათლების სამინისტრო, KAUST, Aramco).
summary.ar: برنامج من موهبة يؤهل طلاب الصف الثاني الثانوي في المملكة للتقديم إلى أفضل 50 جامعة في الولايات المتحدة، عبر التدريب على SAT وكتابة المقالات ودعم طلبات القبول. بعد القبول يتقدم الطلاب للابتعاث لدى جهات شريكة مثل وزارة التعليم وكاوست وأرامكو.

about.en:
Tamayuz (Excellence) is Mawhiba's flagship programme for getting Saudi high-school students into the world's most selective universities, mainly top-ranked US institutions. It targets students in the second year of secondary school and runs through the application season: SAT training, university essay-writing workshops, help completing applications and forms, and individual advising sessions, with an emphasis on STEM majors.

The programme itself provides training only. After admission, students apply to partner sponsors such as the Ministry of Education, KAUST (via KGSP) and Aramco for scholarships to fund their studies. A separate six-week Tamayuz Preparation course for first-year secondary students focuses on the SAT and is optional.

Applicants need averages of at least 90% in grade 9 and grade 10, 90%+ in maths, computer science and science, and an SAT of 1000+ or IELTS Academic 6.5 / TOEFL iBT 80 (SAT holders get priority), plus a personal interview in English. Non-Saudi students can register to benefit from the training content.

en: SAT, essay and application coaching for top US universities
Links to sponsorship from the Ministry of Education, KAUST and Aramco after admission
Individual advising and STEM-major guidance

eligibility.en: Second-year secondary (grade 11) students in Saudi Arabia with 90%+ averages in grades 9 and 10 and in maths/CS/science, plus SAT 1000+ or IELTS 6.5 / TOEFL 80, and a successful interview. Non-Saudis may register to benefit from the training.

en: Log in to the Mawhiba website and confirm your profile.
Register through the Tamayuz service (registration.mawhiba.sa/Tamayuz).
Upload grade 9 and grade 10 certificates plus your SAT or English test report.
Book and pass the English interview once you become a "candidate".
Pay the contribution after acceptance.

costs.en: SAR 4,600 for Mawhiba students (Saudi or Saudi mother, score 1400+ on the Mawhiba scale) and SAR 19,550 for others, each including a refundable SAR 1,150 deposit. Fee exemptions possible with documents.

score_reason: Strong pathway to top US universities and Saudi sponsorship, but paid and closing within days.

org: Mawhiba with the National Center for Assessment (Qiyas)

name.en: Mawhiba National Program for Gifted Identification (Multiple Mental Abilities Test)
name.ka: Mawhiba-ს ნიჭიერთა გამოვლენის ეროვნული პროგრამა (მრავალმხრივი გონებრივი უნარების ტესტი)
name.ar: البرنامج الوطني للكشف عن الموهوبين (مقياس موهبة للقدرات العقلية المتعددة)

deadline_note: Registration closes 28 Dec 2026 per the Mawhiba service page.

summary.en: Saudi Arabia's national gifted-identification test, run by Mawhiba with Qiyas, in Arabic or English for students from grade 3 to the first year of secondary school. Your score unlocks Mawhiba classes, enrichment programmes and university-preparation programmes.
summary.ka: საუდის არაბეთის ეროვნული ნიჭიერების ტესტი, რომელსაც Mawhiba და Qiyas ატარებენ არაბულ ან ინგლისურ ენაზე მე-3 კლასიდან საშუალო სკოლის პირველ კურსამდე. ქულა გიხსნის გზას Mawhiba-ს კლასებზე, გამაძლიერებელ და უნივერსიტეტისთვის მოსამზადებელ პროგრამებზე.
summary.ar: الاختبار الوطني للكشف عن الموهوبين في المملكة، تنفذه موهبة مع قياس باللغتين العربية أو الإنجليزية للطلاب من الصف الثالث الابتدائي حتى الأول الثانوي. تفتح الدرجة الباب لفصول موهبة وبرامجها الإثرائية وبرامج التأهيل للجامعات.

about.en:
The Mawhiba Multiple Mental Abilities Test is the entry point to almost every Mawhiba programme. It is delivered with the National Center for Assessment (Qiyas/ETEC) at test centres across Saudi Arabia, in Arabic or English, at three levels: grades 3–5, grades 6–8 and grades 9–10. Each student can sit the test once per level.

Scores range from 1,000 to 2,000 and stay valid until you move to the next level. Each Mawhiba programme sets its own threshold: Mawhiba classes in partner schools, summer enrichment programmes (such as the Universal Enrichment Program at Saudi universities), the advanced science and maths programme and the Tamayuz top-university preparation programme. Students who do not reach a threshold can still join Mawhiba competitions and retake at the next level.

If you are a student in Saudi Arabia interested in gifted programmes, this test is the first step.

about.en:
The High School Summer Program (HSSP) is KAUST Academy's residential STEM programme for high-achieving secondary students. Each track starts with about two weeks at KAUST in Thuwal and finishes with a week at a UK university. The KAUST–Oxford track (9–30 July 2027) is broad and interdisciplinary: mathematics, programming, physics, chemistry, biology, leadership and collaborative research projects. The KAUST–Cambridge track (about 30 July – 22 August 2027) focuses on advanced mathematics, programming and computational thinking, and innovation projects.

The fee covers return flights, ground transport, accommodation (shared rooms at KAUST, single rooms in the UK, separate housing for boys and girls), full board, tuition, trips, campus facilities and healthcare. After the summer, participants get remote SAT preparation (September–October 2027), an on-campus college admissions camp at KAUST in November 2027 and mentoring on US and UK university applications through March 2028.

Applicants must be at least 15 by the UK flight date. A parent or guardian submits the application between 1 November and 31 December 2026; shortlisted students are interviewed online about their academic interests and readiness. It is expensive, but it combines two world-class campuses with structured university-admissions support.

about.en:
The KAUST Mathematics Competition is a national olympiad-style contest run by KAUST Academy for students in grades 6 to 11 at schools across Saudi Arabia, open to both Saudi nationals and residents. Phase 1 is a two-hour, in-person written test on 23 January 2027 at around 50 centres nationwide (24 multiple-choice questions for grades 6–7 and 8–9, 30 for grades 10–11). Questions are in Arabic and English, and calculators are not allowed.

The top 250 students advance to Phase 2, a three-day event at KAUST in Thuwal on 2–4 April 2027 with a four-hour written-response final, enrichment activities and an awards ceremony. KAUST covers domestic airfare, transport, accommodation and meals for finalists.

Winners receive prizes and free places on KAUST Academy programmes, and first-place winners in grades 8–9 and 10–11 earn an exclusive summer training camp at the University of Cambridge. It is an affordable, high-quality maths competition and a good stepping stone towards national olympiad teams and KAUST's pre-college programmes.

about.en:
STEPs is KAUST Academy's college-preparation programme for Saudi high-school students aiming at the world's leading universities, including the 30 universities on the Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques Scholarship (Arruaad) list. The 2026/27 cycle combines an online component in June 2027, an in-person summer programme at KAUST from 2 July to 11 August 2027, and further online sessions in September–November 2027.

During the summer, mornings are spent on advanced mathematics, programming and SAT training, and afternoons on mentor-guided group projects in a subject of your choice. There is also a speaker series, university-preparation and professional-development lectures, and extracurricular activities on KAUST's Red Sea campus.

Tuition and participation are free, including accommodation and meals during in-person periods; only a SAR 200 application fee applies. Selection is by a 90-minute maths and science admissions test on 19 December 2026 and a personal interview. There is no minimum GPA, but you must be a Saudi national currently in grade 10.

Advanced maths, programming, SAT training and mentored projects
Aimed at admission to top global universities and Arruaad scholarship pathway

about.en:
Khalifa University's Department of Computer Science runs an AI Winter Camp for high-school students during the December school break. The 2026 edition takes place 14–18 December 2026 on KU's main campus in Abu Dhabi and combines lectures, workshops and group projects using real AI tools.

The syllabus covers core AI concepts (machine learning, deep learning, neural networks and natural language processing), applications in healthcare, education and transport, AI for sustainability and social challenges, and career paths in AI, data science, robotics and automation. Students build and train their own machine-learning models, network with KU researchers and receive a certificate of participation.

The camp is free for selected participants, with lunch and snacks provided; bring a laptop. It is aimed at grade 10–12 students with strong science and maths grades and a real interest in AI. Applicants register online (via KU and ADEK channels) and must pass an entry interview. It is a short, free way to get university-level AI exposure and see one of the region's top-ranked engineering universities from the inside.

Good preview of Khalifa University for future applicants

It is free for selected participants, with materials, lunch and snacks provided and a certificate of participation at the end. The programme runs in cohorts across the year, so it suits students exploring which STEM major to choose before university applications.

Only school counsellors can apply on behalf of students, so ask your school's careers or university counsellor to contact KU Outreach.

Government entities, NGOs and companies post opportunities in Arabic and English, from events and community campaigns to environmental, educational and humanitarian work, both on site and virtual.

Students can build a verified record of volunteer hours and download certificates, which is useful for university applications, scholarships and school service requirements (such as IB CAS). Applications to each opportunity are reviewed within about five working days, and volunteering in Abu Dhabi may require a licence from the Department of Community Development, which the platform explains for each posting.

about.en:
Misk Startup School MasterClasses is a free-to-join online learning track on Misk Hub, the youth platform of Saudi Arabia's Misk Foundation. It consists of nine introductory masterclasses taught by founders and investors who have built and scaled startups: Strategic Thinking and Decision Making, Scaling and Growth, Entrepreneurial Mindset, Customer Acquisition, Business Models, Product Management, Market Validation, Funding, and Team.

Each masterclass takes roughly 1.5–2 hours and is self-paced, so you can fit it around school or university. Classes are in English with Arabic subtitles (and sign language). After completing the requirements and the post-assessment survey you can download a Misk certificate of attendance and share it on LinkedIn.

There are no prerequisites; it suits students curious about entrepreneurship, those preparing for startup competitions or incubators, and anyone wanting a structured introduction before joining an accelerator. Enrolment is open until 31 December 2026.

Self-paced, about 2 hours each; English with Arabic subtitles
Misk certificate of attendance

Complete the registration form before 31 December 2026.
Finish the masterclasses and the post-assessment survey to download your certificate.

about.en:
One Million Prompters is a Dubai initiative, backed by the Dubai Future Foundation and the Dubai Centre for Artificial Intelligence, that aims to train one million people in AI and prompt literacy over three years. Its core online course is hands-on and interactive and is split into four modules: Unleashing the Power of AI, Commanding Conversations with AI Chatbots, the AI-Powered Productivity Revolution, and Creative Frontiers with Generative AI (about three hours of video in total).

You learn how large language models and image generators work, how to write effective prompts, and how to use AI tools for study, productivity and creative projects, with a prompt-literacy certification as the learning outcome. The registration form accepts learners of any nationality and country of residence and asks for your school or university, so students are clearly part of the audience.

It is a quick, structured way to get practical AI skills and a credential from a Dubai government-backed initiative; it also links to Dubai's wider prompt-engineering community and events.

Self-paced online; about three hours in total
Open to learners worldwide; prompt-literacy certification

about.en:
The Oxford University Press Story Writing Competition is the Emirates Literature Foundation's flagship writing contest for young people. The 2026/27 theme is "Heroes": what does a hero look like to you? Stories can be written in English or Arabic, and must be original, unpublished and free of AI-generated content.

There are three age groups (age on 10 December 2026): 11 and under (up to 500 words), 12–14 (up to 1,000 words) and 15–18 (up to 1,500 words). Entries open on 9 June 2026 and close at 11:59 pm on 10 December 2026; winners are announced in February 2027 and receive their prizes in April 2027 at the Emirates Airline Festival of Literature in Dubai.

Each category winner receives a plaque, five copies of the published anthology and a free pass to festival sessions, and every entrant gets a certificate of participation. It is free, open to full-time school and homeschool students in the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Bahrain, Kuwait and Oman, and is a good way to get published and recognised at the region's biggest literary festival (winners must attend the Dubai ceremony at their own expense).

There are two age groups (recommended 11 and under, and 12–16) and separate Arabic and English competitions; each school can enter up to two teams per age group per language.

Registration runs 1 September – 10 November 2026. The first round is a virtual written quiz on 2 February 2027; the top 20 teams in each age group then compete in a live final during the Emirates Airline Festival of Literature in Dubai (14–20 April 2027).

There is no registration fee listed, but teams buy the first-round books from Magrudy's. It is open to full-time school and homeschool students in the UAE and the other GCC countries, and it is a fun, team-based way to build reading habits and compete at the region's largest literary festival.

about.en:
Poetry For All, sponsored by Emirates NBD, is the Emirates Literature Foundation's recitation competition. Students learn a poem from the approved list for their age group by heart and perform it on stage without notes; students aged 14–18 also give a short (one-minute) justification of their choice. Categories are 8–13, 14–18 and Students of Determination (8–18), in Arabic or English.

Schools first hold an internal round and then register up to two students per age group per language by 12 November 2026. Semi-finals take place on 11–18 January 2027 in Dubai, 19–21 January in Abu Dhabi, and 25 January in Dubai for Students of Determination. The final round and prize-giving take place during the Emirates Airline Festival of Literature (14–20 April 2027).

It is free and builds public speaking, confidence and a love of poetry; every semi-finalist receives a certificate and winners receive plaques at the festival.

about.en:
The Emirates Literature Foundation's Letter Writing Competition celebrates handwriting and the art of a well-crafted message. For 2027 the theme is "Heroes": write to someone you want to thank, honour or better understand, whether a person you know, a historical figure or a fictional character.

There are three age categories (8–10, 11–13, 14–18). Letters of 200–400 words are handwritten on one side of a single A4 sheet in pen, scanned (not photographed) and uploaded as a PDF through the online form, in Arabic or English. AI-generated content is not allowed. The deadline is 11:59 pm on 8 January 2027.

First-place winners get a meet-and-greet with an Emirates LitFest 2027 author, plus book vouchers, a plaque and a festival pass; all entrants receive a certificate of participation. It is a quick, free entry that suits younger writers.

about.en:
Book in a Box is the Emirates Literature Foundation's class project for primary schools. Guided by their teacher, a class chooses an age-appropriate book and recreates the book, or one scene from it, as a diorama made mainly from recycled or natural materials.

Teachers submit 3–5 photos, a short blurb about the book and why it was chosen through the online form between 1 September 2026 and 25 February 2027. Shortlisted dioramas are displayed at the Emirates Airline Festival of Literature (14–20 April 2027), where final judging (creativity, imagination, originality, use of recycled materials and relevance to the book) and prize-giving take place.

Prizes are plaques and Magrudy's book vouchers (AED 1,000 for first place and the Visitors' Choice award, AED 750 and AED 500 for second and third), and every participant receives a certificate.

The Al-Futtaim Digital Storytelling Competition (Visual Word Award) challenges teams of up to four high-school students aged 14–18 to adapt part of an Arabic book or poem into a 2–3 minute film. Teams can use acting, animation, narration or any creative approach, but the dialogue or narration must be in their own voices in Modern Standard Arabic. Texts come from the competition lists or any published Arabic work linked to sustainability, environment, well-being or cultural diversity.

Films (1080p, 30 fps or more, shot on phones or cameras) are uploaded with a digital poster and a short summary through the online form by 11:59 pm on 2 March 2027. Shortlisted teams meet the judges at the Emirates Airline Festival of Literature in April 2027, where awards are presented.

First place wins the chance to work with a local production studio, a shield and an AED 1,000 book voucher; second and third receive shields and AED 500 vouchers. It is ideal for students interested in film, media and Arabic literature.

summary.en: Abu Dhabi's flagship startup programme for pre-seed to Series A tech companies willing to relocate a founder to Abu Dhabi, with AED 250,000 of in-kind support (office, housing, health insurance, visas) and AED 250,000 cash via a SAFE. Founders from any country can apply.
summary.ka: აბუ-დაბის მთავარი სტარტაპ-პროგრამა pre-seed–Series A ტექნოლოგიური კომპანიებისთვის, რომლებიც თანადამფუძნებელს აბუ-დაბიში გადაიყვანენ: 250 000 დირჰამის ნატურალური მხარდაჭერა (ოფისი, საცხოვრებელი, დაზღვევა, ვიზა) და 250 000 დირჰამი SAFE-ით. განაცხადი ნებისმიერი ქვეყნიდან მიიღება.
summary.ar: البرنامج الرئيسي للشركات الناشئة في أبوظبي للشركات التقنية من مرحلة ما قبل التأسيس حتى الجولة A المستعدة لنقل أحد مؤسسيها إلى أبوظبي، مع دعم عيني بقيمة 250 ألف درهم (مكتب وسكن وتأمين صحي وتأشيرات) و250 ألف درهم نقداً عبر SAFE. يمكن للمؤسسين من أي دولة التقديم.

about.en:
Hub71 is Abu Dhabi's global technology ecosystem, backed by Mubadala and the Abu Dhabi government. Its Access Programme is a 12-month package for pre-seed to Series A startups that want to set up in Abu Dhabi and scale globally: a four-week launch phase, market-entry preparation, growth acceleration (including a three-month guided track powered by Techstars), a fundraising showcase and a public Demo Day.

Selected startups receive AED 250,000 in in-kind incentives (office space, health insurance, housing, licensing and visa support, legal, financial and marketing services) and AED 250,000 in cash in exchange for equity via a SAFE, with a top-up of up to AED 250,000 for high performers. At least one founder must relocate to Abu Dhabi long term and build a team there.

The current deadline is February 2027 for a cohort starting in September 2027; applications are reviewed by April and late applicants are considered for the next cohort. This is a serious option for student or recent-graduate founders with traction who are ready to move to the UAE.

en: AED 250k in-kind support plus AED 250k cash via SAFE
Housing, office, health insurance and visa support in Abu Dhabi
Techstars-powered guided track and Demo Day

eligibility.en: Pre-seed to Series A tech startups from any country. At least one founder must relocate to Abu Dhabi long term. A PDF pitch deck is required.

en: Prepare a PDF pitch deck (problem, solution, traction, team, plans for Abu Dhabi).
Complete the online application at hub71.com/program/access-programme/apply.
If shortlisted, pitch to the Hub71 team and partners in rounds 2 and 3.
Await the selection committee decision (reviews by April 2027).

costs.en: No application fee. Cash investment is in exchange for equity (SAFE note).

score_reason: Generous package open to all nationalities; requires an existing startup and relocation.

summary.ar: المسار التمهيدي في Hub71 للمؤسسين في مرحلة الفكرة أو ما قبل المنتج الأولي: تنضم إلى شريك لبناء المشاريع في أبوظبي وتحصل على رخصة ومكتب مجاناً للسنة الأولى وإرشاد وإمكانية الوصول إلى المنظومة. لا يأخذ Hub71 حصة، لكن شركاء بناء المشاريع يضعون شروطهم الخاصة.

about.en:
Initiate is Hub71's programme for very early founders, at the ideation or pre-MVP stage, which makes it the most accessible Hub71 track for students and recent graduates with a strong idea. Founders apply to one of Hub71's venture-builder partners (such as SC Ventures, Fikra Ventures or TMC2) according to their sector, and the venture builder helps build the MVP and go-to-market strategy.

Hub71 provides a free licence and office space for the first year (the venture builder covers year two), soft-landing guidance in Abu Dhabi, proximity to ADGM's regulatory framework, access to 150+ partners and service providers, and Hub71+ community events. Once milestones are reached, startups can apply to the Hub71 Access Programme.

Priority sectors are FinTech and digital assets, ClimateTech, life sciences, EdTech, mobility and logistics, and FoodTech, with AI-enabled startups encouraged. Hub71 itself takes no equity and gives no direct funding; venture builders set their own funding and equity terms, so read them carefully.

en: For idea and pre-MVP founders
Free licence and office in Abu Dhabi for year one
Pathway to the Hub71 Access Programme

eligibility.en: Early-stage founders at ideation or pre-seed stage building in Hub71 priority sectors (FinTech, ClimateTech, life sciences, EdTech, mobility, FoodTech; AI encouraged). Nationality is not restricted.

en: Choose a venture-builder partner that fits your sector.
Apply via hub71.com/program/initiate/apply.
Pass Hub71's programme-fit check and the venture builder's interviews.
Onboard, relocate/soft-land in Abu Dhabi and start the venture-builder programme.

costs.en: No fee; Hub71 takes no equity. Venture builders usually take equity on their own terms.

score_reason: Rolling and open to all, but requires commitment to build in Abu Dhabi.

about.en:
The Sharjah Entrepreneurship Festival (SEF) is the annual flagship event of Sheraa, the Sharjah government-backed entrepreneurship centre. The 2027 edition takes place on 30–31 January 2027 at SPARK in Sharjah and brings together founders, investors, tech innovators, creatives, aspiring entrepreneurs and students.

The programme typically includes keynote talks and panels, hands-on workshops, an investor lounge, a startup showcase, the Seffy Awards, a children's "Little Founders" area and the SEF Pitch Competition, in which startups pitch for prize funding (advertised at AED 200,000–275,000). It is a strong place for student founders to learn, network and find mentors in the UAE ecosystem.

Passes are sold online with student tickets, and prices increase closer to the event. Sheraa also runs student programmes such as the eight-week Startup Dojo for students and aspiring founders, so the festival is a good entry point into its ecosystem.

en: Two-day festival with talks, workshops and investor networking
SEF Pitch Competition with six-figure AED prize pool
Student passes; gateway to Sheraa's student programmes

eligibility.en: Open to anyone with a pass; student tickets available. Pitch competition is for startups (check the SEF site for criteria and deadline).

en: Buy a festival pass (student pass) on sharjahef.com, early for the lowest price.
If you have a startup, check the SEF Pitch Competition page for the application window.
Plan your sessions and workshops and attend on 30–31 January 2027 at SPARK, Sharjah.

costs.en: Paid passes (student tickets available; price not published on the homepage). Travel and accommodation are your own.

score_reason: Big regional startup event with student passes; paid and in person.

about.en:
Change the World Model United Nations (CWMUN) is a large international MUN circuit run by the Italian non-profit Associazione Diplomatici and Change the World Academy, with conferences in New York, Rome, Paris, Singapore and elsewhere. CWMUN Emirates 2027 will take place in Abu Dhabi in April 2027 (exact dates and venue to be confirmed) for roughly 2,000 students, with the theme "Renewable Energy Diplomacy: a sustainable path to a global future".

There are three age levels: middle school (9–13), high school (14–18) and university (18–28). Participants represent countries in simulated UN committees, and selected students must complete a mandatory online preparatory course before attending. Hotels in Abu Dhabi and Dubai are being arranged by the organiser, and you can register as an individual or with a school/university group.

Admission is selective: you submit an application and do a short interview with Change the World Academy staff. Merit-based grants can reduce enrolment fees or cover conference participation. Airfare and visas are not included; the organiser can issue an invitation letter for the UAE visa.

en: Around 2,000 delegates from many countries; theme Renewable Energy Diplomacy
Middle-school, high-school and university levels
Merit-based grants available; individuals or groups

eligibility.en: Students aged 9–28 of any nationality (middle school, high school or university). Selection interview and completion of the mandatory preparatory course required. English.

en: Submit an application on the CWMUN Emirates page (individual or group).
Complete the selection interview with Change the World Academy staff.
If selected, enrol, apply for a merit grant if needed, and complete the preparatory course.
Arrange your UAE visa (invitation letter available on request) and travel.

costs.en: Enrolment fee (not published on the page) with optional accommodation packages; airfare and visa not included. Merit-based grants can reduce or waive fees.

score_reason: Large international MUN open to all ages and nationalities; fees and exact dates not yet published.

about.en:
TAQADAM is KAUST's startup accelerator, run with SAB (Saudi Awwal Bank) since 2016. It starts with a pre-accelerator bootcamp; teams selected after the bootcamp receive USD 40,000 and enter a six-month programme of mentorship, workshops and in-person activities at KAUST. At the annual showcase, ten startups secure follow-on funding of USD 100,000, and the most promising can qualify for further pre-seed investment.

Teams also get co-working space, subsidised design, finance and legal services, and help incorporating in Saudi Arabia (for international founders). It is open to all nationalities and industries, with no age limit, and accepts both early- and late-stage startups, which makes it accessible to student and graduate founders.

You need at least two founders and evidence of progress (customer interviews or signed interest), at least one founder able to attend all required activities, and university permission if you use university IP. International teams need a realistic plan to expand to Saudi Arabia within a year. Cohort dates are announced on the TAQADAM site; register your interest to be notified.

en: USD 40,000 for teams selected after the bootcamp
USD 100,000 follow-on funding for ten startups at the showcase
Open to all nationalities and ages; co-working at KAUST

eligibility.en: Teams of at least two founders, any nationality, industry or age, with evidence of progress. Not enrolled in another accelerator at bootcamp start. International startups must plan to expand to Saudi Arabia within one year.

en: Register your interest on taqadam.kaust.edu.sa (HubSpot form) or email Apply.Taqadam@kaust.edu.sa.
Apply when the next cohort opens, showing traction and your team.
Attend the pre-accelerator bootcamp if selected.
Teams selected after the bootcamp receive funding and join the six-month programme.

costs.en: No fee listed. Funding terms (USD 40,000 and follow-on) are set by the programme; check equity terms when applying.

score_reason: Well-funded and open to all, but next cohort dates not yet published.

about.en:
Young Future Energy Leaders (YFEL) began in 2010 as part of Masdar Institute's outreach and is now run by Khalifa University in Abu Dhabi. It is a year-long programme for students and young professionals who want to lead in energy and sustainability: participants take a sequence of courses (Foundation, Advanced Exploration, Leadership and Application, the role of policy in renewable energy, entrepreneurship, and being a future leader), along with workshops, debates and panels.

The programme includes case competitions and project sprints, site visits and international engagements, mentorship and career exposure; members traditionally take part in Abu Dhabi Sustainability Week and the World Future Energy Summit. Graduates receive a certificate of completion and join the YFEL alumni community.

It is aimed at advanced undergraduates, master's students and early-career professionals with strong English, from the UAE and abroad. KU lists registration for the 2027 cohort opening on 11 January 2027; check the YFEL site or email yfel@ku.ac.ae for the exact requirements before applying.

en: Year-long energy, climate and policy leadership track
Case competitions, site visits and mentorship
Linked to Abu Dhabi Sustainability Week; certificate and alumni network

eligibility.en: Advanced undergraduate students, master's students and early-career professionals interested in energy and sustainability, from the UAE or abroad. Strong English required.

en: Check the YFEL site for the 2027 call (registration listed as opening 11 January 2027).
Register through KU's portal (pgapply.ku.ac.ae/register/YFEL).
Complete any selection task (past cohorts were selected through a case-study competition).
Attend the programme activities in Abu Dhabi through the year.

costs.en: No fee is listed; participants are responsible for their own travel to Abu Dhabi activities unless KU states otherwise.

score_reason: Respected programme with ADSW links; 2027 dates and eligibility details thin on official pages.

about.en:
Rize UPCG is the Abu Dhabi Department of Education and Knowledge's university-preparation and career-guidance programme for UAE national students in grades 9–12 (years 10–13) across Abu Dhabi. It is designed to help students discover their interests, plan their futures and prepare strong university applications in the UAE and abroad.

The programme has four strands: Future Planning (exploring interests, identifying strengths and building skills); University Guidance (exploring degrees and universities, standardised-test preparation and application support); Counsellor Support (dedicated advisors, career exploration and scholarship applications); and Extracurricular Activities (industry projects, hands-on work experience, portfolio building and ADEK Summer Programs).

It is free and students can register online at any time through the ADEK page. For Emirati students in Abu Dhabi it is one of the most direct routes into ADEK's summer programmes and scholarship guidance.

en: Free university and career guidance with dedicated advisors
Test preparation and application and scholarship support
Access to industry projects and ADEK Summer Programs

eligibility.en: UAE national high-school students in grades 9–12 (years 10–13) in Abu Dhabi.

en: Open the Rize UPCG page on adek.gov.ae.
Click "Register to the Rize UPCG program today!" and complete the form.
Work with your assigned advisor on future planning, testing and applications.

costs.en: Free.

score_reason: Free and useful, but limited to Emirati students in Abu Dhabi.
